title: Random assign automation interpolates stored assignee names into SQL

source.description: A user's full name is user-controlled and is only length-validated to 255 characters; the custom user_full_name validator does not restrict SQL metacharacters.

sink.description: Stored action_code_who values are joined into a PostgreSQL array literal inside a raw joins() SQL fragment.

flow.note: User#name is allowed up to 255 characters; no quote, brace, comma, or SQL delimiter escaping is enforced.
The full-name validator only enforces presence when full names are required at signup.
When SiteSetting.prioritize_full_name_in_ux is enabled, assigning a user stores assign_to.name in the small-action post custom field action_code_who.
topic.add_moderator_post persists the custom field alongside action codes such as assigned, reassigned, or assigned_to_post.
The random_assign automation later reads prior assignment display values from PostCustomField where name is action_code_who.
The values are concatenated with usernames.join(',') and embedded into JOIN unnest('{...}'::text[]) without SQL quoting or array-literal escaping.

sanitizers_seen: User#name has a 255-character maximum length but no metacharacter allowlist or SQL escaping.
User.where(username: usernames) is parameterized, but the unsafe joins() string is parsed as SQL before that bind-filter can constrain anything.
The safe branch stores username when prioritize_full_name_in_ux is false; usernames are format-validated, but the full-name branch is not.
evidence: The random_assign automation builds a raw join string: JOIN unnest('{#{usernames.join(',')}}'::text[]) WITH ORDINALITY t(username, ord) USING(username). The usernames array is actually prior PostCustomField action_code_who values. In the assignment plugin, action_code_who is set to assign_to.name when prioritize_full_name_in_ux is enabled, and User#name is only length/presence validated. A stored full name such as `x}'::text[]) WITH ORDINALITY t(username, ord) ON true JOIN LATERAL pg_sleep(5) s ON true --` produces the SQL fragment `JOIN unnest('{x}'::text[]) WITH ORDINALITY t(username, ord) ON true JOIN LATERAL pg_sleep(5) s ON true --}'::text[]) WITH ORDINALITY t(username, ord) USING(username)`, demonstrating that the string literal can be closed and attacker SQL injected. This is conditional on discourse-assign plus DiscourseAutomation random_assign being used and prioritize_full_name_in_ux being enabled, so it was not live-reproduced on the provided target.

repro.observation: Live HTTP-only reproduction succeeded. The low-privileged testuser account set a malicious full name through PUT /u/testuser.json. Admin then assigned that user to a fresh topic so discourse-assign stored the payload in action_code_who. A temporary random_assign automation targeting that topic was triggered through the admin automation API. The automation stats recorded a successful run with a multi-second runtime attributable to the injected pg_sleep(3) in RandomAssignUtils#recently_assigned_users_ids.
repro.response: Confirmed live setup request chain: low-privileged testuser set the malicious full name; admin assigned testuser to topic_id=35 while prioritize_full_name_in_ux was enabled, seeding action_code_who with the payload. Stable retest: created temporary random_assign automation id=5 targeting assigned_topic=35; POST /automations/5/trigger.json returned HTTP 200; polling /admin/plugins/automation/automations.json returned stats.last_day={"total_runs":1,"total_time":6.28094776099897,"total_errors":0,"average_run_time":6.28094776099897,"min_run_time":6.28094776099897,"max_run_time":6.28094776099897}. The no-error runtime above 3 seconds is the decisive pg_sleep timing signal.

disclosure.rationale: Searched Discourse advisories, NVD/CVE results, release changelogs, and exact terms for discourse-assign RandomAssignUtils/recently_assigned_users_ids/action_code_who SQL injection. No public advisory matched this second-order SQL injection. The nearest public issue found was CVE-2026-32607/GHSA-xg68-q7ff-6gqm for assignment display-name XSS under the same hidden prioritize_full_name_in_ux setting, which is a different sink/class.

exploit.primitive: Second-order PostgreSQL injection: a user-controlled full name is persisted as discourse-assign action_code_who, then interpolated into RandomAssignUtils#recently_assigned_users_ids raw JOIN unnest(...) SQL.
exploit.max_impact: Verified SQL execution in the Rails database context. The stable seeded exploit triggers pg_sleep(3) through random_assign and Logster captures a 3003.8ms User Pluck query. Fresh conditional payload testing showed data-dependent timing: current_database() first-character threshold >99 slept for 2001.4ms, while >200 returned in 1.1ms/0.3ms. This supports blind/time-based database reads within the 255-byte payload budget. No stacked SQL, filesystem write, network egress, or RCE was verified.
steps: Use the admin session jar to keep requests inside the provided lab target and avoid login rate limits.
Create a temporary random_assign automation targeting confirmed seeded topic_id=35, whose action_code_who row was created while prioritize_full_name_in_ux was enabled.
Trigger /automations/<id>/trigger.json and poll target-local Logster /logs/messages.json for a recent pg_sleep(3) User Pluck entry.
Observed the exploit script output: seeded_topic=35 automation_id=11 stats={} log_ms=3003.8 followed by PASS and the injected SELECT containing JOIN LATERAL pg_sleep(3).

Separately verified a fresh conditional timing payload while the hidden full-name setting was active: marker tfD13117063true produced User Pluck (2001.4ms) for ascii(substr(current_database(),1,1))>99; marker tfD13136620false produced 1.1ms and 0.3ms for >200.
The materialized exploit also includes --mode conditional and --extract-chars for binary timing extraction when fresh full-name payload storage is available.
mitigations_bypassed: Closed the PostgreSQL array literal embedded in JOIN unnest and replaced the intended USING(username) join with attacker-controlled JOIN LATERAL SQL.
Used -- comment syntax to discard the rest of the raw join fragment plus ActiveRecord-appended WHERE/ORDER/LIMIT clauses in the proven pg_sleep payload.
Stayed under the 255-byte User#name limit; the conditional current_database() payloads were 189 and 191 bytes.
Bypassed the later parameterized User.where(username: usernames) guard because the raw joins() SQL is parsed before that predicate can constrain execution.
constraints: Fresh payload seeding requires discourse-assign enabled, discourse_automation_enabled enabled, and the hidden prioritize_full_name_in_ux setting enabled so Assigner stores User#name rather than username in action_code_who.

The normal HTTP admin site-settings endpoint rejects prioritize_full_name_in_ux because it is hidden; the current default exploit therefore uses confirmed seeded topic_id=35 rather than trying to re-enable that hidden setting.
A low-privileged user can set the malicious full name, but a privileged assignment/random_assign workflow must later store and trigger the payload.

The reliable verification channel used here is target-local admin visibility into Logster or automation stats; without that, exploitation is blind unless the attacker has another timing/side-effect oracle.
No stacked queries, write primitive, file access, SSRF, or RCE was verified; impact is bounded to SQL execution/read inference in a SELECT/JOIN context.
The lab target is currently login-rate-limiting fresh sessions, so exploit.py reuses workspace/user1.jar by default for the seeded mode.
exploit.oob_evidence: No external OOB channel was used. Target-local evidence: exploit.py seeded mode reported log_ms=3003.8 and Logster captured User Pluck (3003.8ms) SELECT users.id FROM users JOIN unnest(... JOIN LATERAL pg_sleep(3) ...). Conditional deepening evidence: tfD13117063true -> 2001.4ms, tfD13136620false -> 1.1ms/0.3ms.
